newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher, but gains concentrated.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher, but gains concentrated.

text.p: Taiwan share prices fought off late profit-taking to close higher on Friday, but the gains were concentrated narrowly on the financial sector and brokers said the market now might ease into a consolidation.
The weighted index gained 43.25 points or 0.55 percent to close at 7,875.32. Turnover was a frantic T$139.35 billion despite Friday's being a public holiday outside the markets.
Earlier in the session the market had reached a high of 7,923.81 on momentum from a two-month rally that had boosted the index by more than 1,000 points in 1997.
But late profit-taking erased some of the early gains.
The heavily weighted financials gained 1.74 percent while industrials slipped 0.05 percent on profit-taking.

"There was concern that the market was only being supported by financials, and that industrials weren't doing their part," said Taiwan Securities Investment analyst Joe Chiou. "If this trend continues the market will have little room to rise more."
The market's big 1997 surge has been fuelled by expectations that Taiwan's sluggish economic recovery was gaining steam.
The "Big Three" state-run commercial banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan, rose T$6, T$5 and T$3.50 respectively to T$178, T$182 and T$146.
Brokers said they expected the index to fluctuate in a narrow 7,820-7,920 range in Saturday's shortened session.

Analysts said Friday's high turnover showed the market had avoided any fallout from a three-day tempest over whether the financial markets should close on Friday and Saturday to mark a new holiday commemorating a February 28, 1947, massacre.
Parliament enacted the holiday only on Tuesday and included plans for the markets to close, sparking howls of protest from businesses worried about disruptions and lost productivity.
The cabinet on Thursday abruptly reversed the closing plan, saying banks and financial markets would open both days.
